In-house markerless multi-camera body capture

Four Regions

Head, neck, feet and fingers — drawn from the delivered subject-*.body-track.npz, not from a run held in memory. Colour is not decoration here: it is the provenance of each joint, and the three colours are three different claims.

The feet were the interesting one, and not for the reason expected. The delivered foot was assigned the torso’s orientation — it swung when the chest swung and carried no foot information at all. That is worse than a frozen joint, because a constant is visibly degenerate while a foot moving with the chest passes any “does it move?” check and reads fine in an overlay.

Nothing observed could have constrained it: the 19 landmark targets stop at the ankle. The ball of the foot supplies the missing axis, and it is the only new landmark in this pass that survived measurement — the toe tip fails at 12.8–63.3% and is deliberately unused, so the toes ride the foot rather than getting a joint they cannot support.

Check: the rig’s foot axis now agrees with the measured ankle-to-ball direction to 1.7–3.2°, and the rig’s ankle angle reads 67.3–70.9° against 67.4–71.2° measured.

Why the fingers get a pose and not a solve

The detector emits 15 finger joints per hand, and they give themselves away on length rather than stability. Every finger segment measures roughly half its anatomical size — the palm reads 39–58 mm where a hand is 85–100, the index-to-pinky span 35–44 mm where it should be 65–85. The hand is being collapsed toward the wrist. A segment that is stable in the wrong place is a prediction, not a measurement.

So they get a relaxed curl instead — and the point is that the alternative was never neutral. Leaving all 30 joints at the identity is also an invented pose, and a worse one: it splays the hand into a rigid claw no resting human makes. Both are uncaptured. This one is anatomically right, and it is labelled.

What this page is blind to

Everything here is self-consistency, never accuracy. No number in this project has been checked against ground truth, so a foot that agrees with its own landmark to 1.7° is a correctly implemented frame, not a correctly placed one. The head passes its gate on one performer of two. A 3D view proves placement in the world it was solved in and can never prove the world was right.
